:::{#exm-information-poisson}
#### Information for Poisson data

For $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$,
one observation's score is $x/\rate - 1$ (@exr-pois-score-fn),
whose derivative with respect to $\rate$ is $-x/\rate^2$.
Summing over the observations (@thm-deriv-llik-iid),
the Hessian is $\hess = -\sumin x_i / \rate^2$, so:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\oinf(\rate)
&= -\hess
&& \text{(observed information: negative Hessian)}\\
&= -\paren{-\frac{\sumin x_i}{\rate^2}}
&& \text{(substitute the Hessian)}\\
&= \frac{\sumin x_i}{\rate^2}
&& \text{(two negatives make a positive)}\\
\einf(\rate)
&= \E{\frac{\sumin X_i}{\rate^2}}
&& \text{(expected information)}\\
&= \frac{\E{\sumin X_i}}{\rate^2}
&& \text{(factor the constant $\tfrac{1}{\rate^2}$ out of the expectation)}\\
&= \frac{\sumin \E{X_i}}{\rate^2}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \frac{\sumin \rate}{\rate^2}
&& \text{($\E{X_i} = \rate$)}\\
&= \frac{n\rate}{\rate^2}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\rate$)}\\
&= \frac{n}{\rate}
&& \text{(cancel one factor of $\rate$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
